$comment: Allowlist for `scripts/check-known-advisories.mjs`, the gate over the snap's
TRANSITIVE production dependency graph. It is the machine-readable form of
the dependency table in docs/THREAT-MODEL.md section 5, so that table stops
being prose a reviewer has to remember to re-derive.
Entries are keyed by MODULE, not by advisory ID, and that is deliberate. The
security property being asserted is 'this package does not reach the shipped
bundle', which is a property of the package. Keying by advisory ID would mean
a new axios CVE (there were 28 at the last count, and the number only goes up)
turns the build red without telling anyone anything new, which trains people
to edit the allowlist without thinking. Keying by module means a new advisory
in an ALREADY-UNREACHABLE package is silent, while an advisory in any package
not listed here fails the build and demands a decision.
`absentFromBundle: true` is not a claim taken on trust: the script searches
the built dist/bundle.js for that package's `bundleMarkers` and fails if any
of them turns up. A package that genuinely does ship must instead be listed
with `inBundle: true` and a written justification, which is the entry a
reviewer should always stop at.
WHY MARKERS RATHER THAN PACKAGE NAMES. The obvious check is to search the
bundle for the package name, and that is what this file's gate used to do. It
cannot work: `mm-snap build` emits a minified bundle in which package names do
not survive. Measured on the 0.1.0 bundle, the strings `stellar-base` and
`@noble` are both absent while both packages demonstrably ship. A zero-hit
result therefore carried no information, and the gate would have passed
unchanged on the day a dependency bump started pulling axios into the bundle.
A marker must be a STRING LITERAL from the package's runtime code (an error
message, a header name, a protocol constant). Identifiers, class names, and
file paths are renamed or stripped by minification; string literals are not.
Prefer several markers per package so a single upstream reword cannot silently
disarm the check, and re-derive them whenever the parent dependency crosses a
major version.
WHY POSITIVE CONTROLS. Markers only prove absence if the search would have
found them had they been there. `positiveControls` are markers from packages
that certainly DO ship; the script requires every one of them to be found. If
one goes missing, the bundling or minification behaviour has changed in a way
that may also have disarmed the absence checks, so the script fails rather
than reporting a clean result it can no longer justify. This is what keeps the
gate honest about its own power.
WHAT THE YARN AUDIT FEEDING THIS GATE DOES AND DOES NOT MEASURE. The vendored
Yarn 3 builds its audit map keyed by package NAME across every workspace in the
monorepo, so when two workspaces resolve different versions of one package,
a single version wins and is reported as if it were the snap's. Measured on
this repository: the snap resolves axios 1.18.0 (with follow-redirects 1.16.0
and form-data 4.0.6) through @stellar/stellar-sdk, the site resolves axios
1.12.1 through gatsby, and `yarn npm audit` run from packages/snap reports the
1.12.1 advisories with a path through the stellar SDK. The three entries below
therefore disposition advisories that may not be the snap's, and the same
mechanism would under-report if the roles reversed. That is why the entries
are keyed by module and why this file is not the only gate:
scripts/check-snap-graph-advisories.mjs computes the snap's exact
lockfile-resolved production closure from Yarn's own resolution of the
workspace and audits those versions against the registry directly. Its
allowlist is this same `modules` map. The yarn-fed gate keeps its distinct job,
which is to prove through `bundleMarkers` that these packages are absent from
the artifact that ships, whichever version any workspace resolved.

positiveControls.reason: The Asset constructor's validation message. stellar-base is the core of what this snap bundles, so if this string is missing the bundle is not what this script thinks it is.

positiveControls.marker: Invalid private key: Value is not a valid
positiveControls.reason: SLIP10Node's private-key assertion. Key derivation is the one subsystem that cannot possibly have been tree-shaken out of a signing snap.

axios.reason: The snap hand-rolls its fetch-based Horizon and Soroban RPC client (src/stellar/http.ts, horizon.ts, rpc.ts) and never imports the SDK's Horizon or webauth modules, so webpack tree-shakes the entire axios subtree out of the bundle.

bundleMarkers: FormData boundary must be a string
form-data.reason: Reached only through axios, which is itself absent. See the axios entry. The snap's own submission path posts application/x-www-form-urlencoded via URLSearchParams and constructs no multipart body.

follow-redirects.reason: Reached only through axios, which is itself absent. See the axios entry. Note the snap sets `redirect: 'error'` on every fetch it makes, so it does not follow redirects by any path.
